body:
PR #4049 does steps 1, 2 and 4. Two corrections to what I wrote above.

**The cloud sweep came back clean — the blocker was smaller than I assumed.** I said it "has to happen there" and that I couldn't see the repo; I could, and it took one pass. `cloud` touches share-links in exactly two places (`objectos-runtime/src/artifact-kernel-factory.ts`, `service-cloud/src/default-environment-plugins.ts`), and both only **register** `SharingServicePlugin` into a per-environment kernel with `registerShareLinkRoutes: false` — precisely so this dispatcher serves the paths. No calls to the endpoints, no body reads, no `body.link` / `body.links` in the repo at all.

**Step 2 was wrong about the status.** "Drop the duplicate keys and route both through `deps.success(...)`" only works for list. `deps.success` hardcodes status 200, and `POST /share-links` is a **201** — which is the same reason the `/keys` domain hand-builds its own 201. So create stays hand-built (minus the duplicate key, matching `/keys`' shape) and list moves onto the helper.

**Step 3 I'm declining, and it was my recommendation, so worth saying why.** I wrote that deleting objectui's `body.links ?? body.data` was "worth doing even if 1–2 are deferred", because a tolerance kept past its reason reads as "both shapes are still live".

That conflates two different things. Before #3983 this was **drift** — two live producers genuinely disagreeing, and the consumer had to sniff. After #3983 and this PR it is **version skew** — one producer changed, and the consumer still supports the older one. Those want opposite treatment: drift should be deleted at the producer (which is what these PRs did), skew should be kept until a version gate retires it.

Concretely: `@object-ui/components` publishes standalone against peer deps, so a new console can meet an older framework. Dropping the `??` turns that case from *working* into a **silently empty share list** — no error, no empty-state, just no links. That's a poor trade for removing one `??`. It should go when there's a declared minimum framework version to hang it on, not before.

Leaving this issue to close with #4049; step 3 is not part of it.
